Lin, after passing the examination supplemented Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Assistant Magistrate of Lantian. In the Qianning era he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
86
嚴，字凜之，會昌四年進士擢第。 是歲僕射王起典貢部，選士三十人，嚴與楊知至、竇緘、源重、鄭樸五人試文合格，物議以子弟非之，起覆奏。 武宗敕曰：「楊嚴一人可及第，余四人落下。」 嚴釋褐諸侯府。 咸通中，累遷吏部員外，轉郎中，拜給事中、工部侍郎，尋以本官充翰林學士。 兄收作相，封章請外職，拜越州刺史、御史中丞、浙東團練觀察使。 收罷相貶官，嚴坐貶邵州刺史。 收得雪，嚴量移吉王傅。 乾符四年，累遷兵部侍郎。 五年，判度支。 其年病卒。 二子：涉、注。
Yan, styled Linzhi, in the fourth year of Huichang passed the jinshi selection. That year Vice Director Wang Qi presided over the examination department and selected thirty candidates; Yan with Yang Zhizhi, Dou Jian, Yuan Zhong, and Zheng Pu passed the literary test; public opinion criticized them as sons of officials; Qi resubmitted. Emperor Wuzong's edict read, "Yang Yan alone may pass; the other four are rejected." Yan left office in feudal headquarters. In the Xiantong era he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Personnel, transferred Director, appointed Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Public Works, and soon with his existing office served as Hanlin Academician. When elder brother Shou became chief minister he submitted sealed memorial requesting an outer post and was appointed Prefect of Yue, Censor-in-Chief, and Zhedong Training-and-Observation Commissioner. When Shou was removed as chief minister and demoted, Yan was implicated and demoted Prefect of Shao. When Shou was cleared Yan was transferred in measure to Tutor of the Prince of Ji. In the fourth year of Qianfu he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War. In the fifth year he directed the Revenue Bureau. That year he died of illness. Two sons: She and Zhu.
87
涉，乾符二年登進士第。 昭宗朝，累遷吏部郎中、禮、刑二侍郎。 乾符四年，改吏部侍郎。 天祐初，轉左丞。 從昭宗遷洛陽，改吏部尚書。 輝王即位，本官平章事，加中書侍郎。 涉性端厚秉禮。 乾寧之後，賊臣竊發，王室浸微。 及天祐東遷，大事去矣。 涉為時所嬰，不能自退。 及命相之日，與家人相向灑泣曰：「吾不能脫此網羅，禍將至矣。」 謂其子凝式曰：「今日之命，吾家重不幸矣，必累爾等。」 涉謙退善處，竟以令終。
She, in the second year of Qianfu passed the jinshi examination. In the Zhaozong court he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Vice Minister of Rites and Justice. In the fourth year of Qianfu he was reassigned Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel. At the beginning of Tianyou he was transferred Left Vice Director. Following Emperor Zhaozong to Luoyang he was reassigned Minister of Personnel. When Prince Hui acceded, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister and was added Vice Director of the Secretariat. She was upright, thick, and observant of ritual. After Qianning treacherous ministers arose and the royal house gradually declined. When Tianyou moved east the great affair was lost. She was bound by the times and could not withdraw himself. On the day he was appointed chief minister he faced his family weeping together, saying, "I cannot escape this net; calamity will soon arrive." He told his son Ningshi, "Today's appointment is heavy misfortune for our family; it will surely implicate you all." She was modest and good at comportment and in the end had a good end.
88
注，中和二年進士登第。 昭宗朝，累官考功員外、刑部郎中。 尋知制誥，正拜中書舍人，召充翰林學士，累遷戶部侍郎。 輝王纘歷，兄涉為宰相，注避嫌辭內職，守戶部侍郎。
Zhu, in the second year of Zhonghe passed the jinshi examination. In the Zhaozong court he rose repeatedly to Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Personnel and Director in the Ministry of Justice. Soon he directed proclamations, was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, summoned Hanlin Academician, and repeatedly promoted Vice Minister of Revenue. When Prince Hui succeeded the throne and elder brother She was chief minister, Zhu avoided suspicion and resigned inner duties, serving as Vice Minister of Revenue.
89
韋保衡者，字蘊用，京兆人。 祖元貞，父愨，皆進士登第。 愨，字端士，太和初登第，後累佐使府，入朝亟歷臺閣。 大中四年，拜禮部侍郎。 五年選士，頗得名人，載領方鎮節度，卒。
Wei Baoheng, styled Yunyong, was a native of the capital district. His grandfather Yuanzhen and father Que both passed the jinshi examination. Que, styled Duanshi, at the beginning of Taihe passed the examination and later repeatedly served in headquarters and entered court, quickly passing through the censorate. In the fourth year of Dazhong he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites. In the fifth year he selected candidates and obtained many famous men; he also served as regional military commissioner and died.
90
保衡，咸通五年登進士第，累拜起居郎。 十年正月，尚懿宗女同昌公主。 公主郭淑妃所生，妃有寵，出降之日，傾宮中珍玩以為贈送之資。 尋以保衡為翰林學士，轉郎中，正拜中書舍人、兵部侍郎，承旨。 不期年，以本官平章事。
Baoheng, in the fifth year of Xiantong passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly appointed Attendant of the Palace Secretariat. In the first month of the tenth year he married Emperor Yizong's daughter, Princess Tongchang. The princess was born to Consort Guo Shufei; the consort was favored, and on the day of the marriage the palace's precious curios were emptied as dowry gifts. Soon Baoheng was made Hanlin Academician, transferred Director, formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of War, and Drafting Commissioner. Within less than a year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister.
91
保衡恃恩權，素所不悅者，必加排斥。 王鐸貢舉之師，蕭遘同門生，以素薄其為人，皆擯斥之。 以楊收、路巖在中書不加禮接，媒孽逐之。 自起居郎至宰相，二年之間，階至特進、扶風縣開國侯、食邑二千戶、集賢殿大學士。 十一年八月，公主薨，自後恩禮漸薄。 咸通末，淮、徐盜起，素所怨者發其陰事，保衡竟得罪賜死。
Baoheng relied on favor and power; those he disliked he always excluded. Wang Duo was his examination teacher and Xiao Zui his fellow student; because he had always thought little of them as men, he excluded them both. Because Yang Shou and Lu Yan were in the Secretariat and did not show him courtesy, he slandered and drove them away. From Attendant of the Palace Secretariat to chief minister, within two years his rank rose to Special Advancement, Marquis of Fufeng with a fief of two thousand households, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. In the eighth month of the eleventh year the princess died; thereafter favor gradually thinned. At the end of Xiantong, when Huai and Xu bandits arose, those he had long resented exposed his secret affairs and Baoheng in the end was condemned and ordered to die.
92
弟保乂，進士登第，尚書郎、知制誥，召充翰林學士，歷禮、戶、兵三侍郎、學士承旨。 坐保衡免官。
Younger brother Baoyi passed the jinshi examination, served Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer for Proclamations, was summoned Hanlin Academician, and passed through Vice Ministers of Rites, Revenue, and War and Drafting Commissioner. Because of Baoheng he was removed from office.
93
路巖者，字魯瞻，陽平寇氏人也。 祖季登，大歷六年登進士第，累辟諸侯府。 升朝為尚書郎，遷左諫議大夫，卒。 生三子，群、庠、單，皆登進士第。
Lu Yan, styled Luzhan, was a native of the Kou clan of Yangping. His grandfather Jideng, in the sixth year of Dali passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to feudal headquarters. He entered court as Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was transferred Left Remonstrator, and died. He had three sons—Qun, Xiang, and Shan—all of whom passed the jinshi examination.
94
群，字正夫，既擢進士，又書判拔萃，累佐使府。 入朝為監察御史。 穆宗初即位，遣使西北邊犒宴軍士，稱旨，累加兵部郎中。 太和二年，遷諫議大夫，以本官充侍講學士。 四年，罷侍講為翰林學士。 五年，正拜中書舍人，學士如故。
Qun, styled Zhengfu, having passed the jinshi also distinguished himself in document judgment and repeatedly served in headquarters. He entered court as Attending Censor. When Emperor Muzong first acceded he was sent as envoy to feast frontier soldiers in the northwest and pleased the emperor; he was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of War. In the second year of Taihe he was transferred Remonstrator and with his existing office served as Lecturer-in-Attendance. In the fourth year he was removed as lecturer and made Hanlin Academician. In the fifth year he was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, continuing as academician.
95
群精經學，善屬文。 性仁孝，誌行貞潔。 父母歿後，終身不茹葷血。 歷踐臺閣，受時君異寵，未嘗以勢位自矜。 與士友結交，榮達如一。 八年正月病卒，君子惜之。 二子：嶽、巖，大中中相次進士登第。
Qun was skilled in classical learning and good at composing prose. By nature he was benevolent and filial, his will and conduct pure. After his parents died he never ate flesh or blood for the rest of his life. Passing through the censorate he received the contemporary ruler's special favor and never prided himself on power and rank. In befriending scholars and friends he treated honor and success the same. In the first month of the eighth year he died of illness; gentlemen regretted it. Two sons: Yue and Yan, who in Dazhong successively passed the jinshi examination.
96
巖，幼聰敏過人，父友踐方鎮，書幣交辟，久之方就。 數年之間，出入禁署。 累遷中書舍人、戶部侍郎。 咸通三年，以本官同平章事，年始三十六。 在相位八年，累兼左僕射。 懿宗時，王政多僻，宰臣用事。 巖既承委遇，稍務奢靡，頗通賂遺。 及韋保衡尚公主，素惡巖為人。 保衡作相，罷巖知政事，以檢校左僕射出為成都尹、劍南西川節度使。 未幾，改荊南節度。 詔令六月下峽赴鎮，尋復罷之。
Yan from youth was clever beyond others; his father's friends who served as regional commissioners repeatedly sent letters summoning him, and only after a long time did he go. Within several years he entered and left the forbidden secretariat. He was repeatedly promoted Gentleman of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Revenue. In the third year of Xiantong, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister at age thirty-six. In the chief-minister position eight years he was repeatedly concurrent Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works. In Emperor Yizong's time royal governance was often perverse and chief ministers wielded power. Yan, having received entrusted favor, gradually pursued extravagance and quite trafficked in bribes. When Wei Baoheng married the princess he had always disliked Yan as a man. When Baoheng became chief minister he removed Yan from governing affairs and sent him out as Acting Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Chief of Chengdu, and Western Chuan Military Commissioner. Before long he was reassigned Jingnan Military Commissioner. An edict ordered him to leave the gorges in the sixth month and proceed to his command; soon he was again removed.
97
嶽，歷兩郡刺史，入為給事中。 子德延。
Yue served successively as prefect of two prefectures and entered court as Supervising Censor. His son was Deyan.
98
夏侯孜，字好學，本譙人。 父審封。 孜，寶歷二年登進士第，釋褐諸侯府，累遷婺、絳二郡刺史。 入為諫議大夫，轉給事中。 十年，改刑部侍郎。 十一年，兼御史中丞，遷尚書右丞、上柱國，賜紫金魚袋。 十一年二月，遷朝議大夫，守戶部侍郎，判戶部事。 再加兵部侍郎，充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使。 懿宗即位，以本官同平章事，領使如故。 累加左僕射、門下侍郎，封譙郡侯，與路巖、楊收同輔政。 咸通八年，罷相，檢校司空、同平章事，兼成都尹，充劍南西川節度使。 屬南蠻入寇，蜀中饑饉，軍儲不備，蠻陷巂州，蜀川大擾。 尋移孜為河中尹、檢校司徒、河中晉絳節度使。
Xiahou Zi, styled Haoxue, was originally from Qiao. His father was Shenfeng. Zi, in the second year of Baoli passed the jinshi examination, left office in feudal headquarters, and was repeatedly promoted Prefect of Wu and Jiang. He entered court as Remonstrator and transferred Supervising Censor. In the tenth year he was reassigned Vice Minister of Justice. In the eleventh year he was concurrent Censor-in-Chief, transferred Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Pillar of State, and granted the purple-gold fish pouch. In the second month of the eleventh year he was transferred Grand Master of the Court for Discussion, serving as Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of Revenue Bureau affairs. He was again added Vice Minister of War and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport for All Circuits. When Emperor Yizong acceded, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister and continued as commissioner. He was repeatedly added Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Marquis of Qiao; with Lu Yan and Yang Shou he jointly assisted governance. In the eighth year of Xiantong he was removed as chief minister, appointed Acting Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister, concurrent Chief of Chengdu, and Western Chuan Military Commissioner. When southern barbarians invaded, Shu suffered famine and military stores were not prepared; the barbarians captured Xi Prefecture and the Sichuan region was greatly disturbed. Soon Zi was transferred Chief of Hezhong, Acting Minister of Education, and Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner.
99
九年，龐勛據徐州，南蠻深入。 天子懲孜治蜀無政，詔曰：
In the ninth year Pang Xun held Xu Prefecture and southern barbarians penetrated deeply. The Son of Heaven, reproaching Zi for governing Shu without effective policy, issued an edict saying:
100
未幾卒。
Before long he died.
101
子潭、澤，皆登進士第。 潭，累官至禮部侍郎。 中和三年選士，多至卿相。 子坦。
His sons Tan and Ze both passed the jinshi examination. Tan rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of Rites. In the third year of Zhonghe he selected candidates; many rose to chief ministers. His son was Tan.
102
劉瞻，字幾之，彭城人。 祖升，父景。 瞻，太和初進士擢第。 四年，又登博學宏詞科，歷佐使府。 咸通初升朝，累遷太常博士。 劉瑑作相，以宗人遇之，薦為翰林學士。 轉員外郎中，正拜中書舍人、戶部侍郎，承旨。 出為太原尹、河東節度使。 入拜京兆尹，復為戶部侍郎、翰林學士。 十年，以本官同平章事，加中書侍郎，兼刑部尚書、集賢殿大學士。
Liu Zhan, styled Jizhi, was a native of Pengcheng. His grandfather was Sheng and his father Jing. Zhan, at the beginning of Taihe passed the jinshi selection. In the fourth year he also passed the Broad Learning and Grand Words examination and repeatedly served in headquarters. At the beginning of Xiantong he entered court and was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of Ceremonies. When Liu Zhuan became chief minister he treated him as a clansman and recommended him Hanlin Academician. He transferred Outer Court Attendant and Director, was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Revenue, and Drafting Commissioner. He was sent out Chief of Taiyuan and Hedong Military Commissioner. He entered court as Chief of the Capital and again became Vice Minister of Revenue and Hanlin Academician. In the tenth year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister, added Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Justice, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
103
十一年八月，同昌公主薨，懿宗尤嗟惜之。 以翰林醫官韓宗召、康仲殷等用藥無效，收之下獄。 兩家宗族，枝蔓盡捕三百余人，狴牢皆滿。 瞻召諫官令上疏，無敢極言。 瞻自上疏曰：
In the eighth month of the eleventh year Princess Tongchang died and Emperor Yizong especially lamented her. Because Hanlin medical officers Han Zongzhao, Kang Zhongyin, and others used medicine without effect, they were arrested and imprisoned. The two families' clans and branches—all more than three hundred persons—were captured; the prisons were full. Zhan summoned remonstrators and ordered them to submit memorials; none dared speak to the utmost. Zhan himself submitted a memorial saying:
104
自陛下雷霆一怒，朝野震驚，囚九族於狴牢，因兩人之藥誤。 老幼械系三百余人，咸云：「宗召荷恩之日，寸祿不沾，進藥之時，又不同議。 此乃禍從天降，罪匪己為。」 物議沸騰，道路嗟嘆。
Since Your Majesty's thunderous rage, court and countryside were shaken; nine clans were imprisoned and because of two men's mistaken medicine. Old and young in shackles, more than three hundred persons, all said, "On the day Zongzhao received grace not a foot of salary was touched; when medicine was administered he likewise did not jointly discuss. This is calamity falling from heaven—the crime is not self-wrought." Public opinion boiled and people on the roads sighed.
105
陛下以寬仁厚德，禦宇十年，四海萬邦，鹹歌聖政。 何事遽移前誌，頓易初心。 以達理知命之君，涉肆暴不明之謗。 且殉宮女而違道，囚平人而結冤，此皆陛下安不思危，忿不顧難者也。
Your Majesty, with generous benevolence and thick virtue, has ruled the realm ten years; within the four seas and ten thousand states all sing of sacred governance. Why suddenly shift the former resolve and abruptly change the original heart? For a ruler who knows fate through reason, to involve reckless cruelty and unclear blame. Moreover to follow a palace woman's death against the Way and imprison common people to knot enmity—these are cases where Your Majesty is secure without thinking of danger and angry without considering difficulty.
106
陛下信崇釋典，留意生天，大要不過喜舍慈悲，方便布施，不生惡念，所謂福田。 則業累盡消，往生忉利，比居濁惡，未可同年。 伏望陛下盡釋系囚，易怒為喜，虔奉空王之教，以資愛主之靈。 中外臣僚，同深懇激。
Your Majesty trusts and honors the Buddhist canon and attends to rebirth in heaven; the great essentials are nothing beyond delighting in giving, compassion, convenient generosity, and not giving rise to evil thoughts—the so-called field of merit. Then accumulated karma is entirely extinguished and one is reborn in Trayastrimsha—compared with dwelling in turbid wickedness it cannot be matched in the same year. We humbly hope Your Majesty will fully release the imprisoned, easily change anger to joy, and reverently follow the Empty King's teaching to support the spirit of loving the ruler. Inside and outside, ministers and officials alike deeply urge this.
107
帝閱疏大怒，即日罷瞻相位，檢校刑部尚書、同平章事、江陵尹，充荊南節度等使。 再貶康州刺史，量移虢州刺史。 入朝為太子賓客分司。 翰林學士戶部侍郎鄭畋、右諫議大夫高湘、比部郎中知制誥楊知至、禮部郎中魏纻、兵部員外張顏、刑部員外崔彥融、御史中丞孫瑝等，皆坐瞻親善貶逐。 京兆尹溫璋仰藥而卒。
The emperor read the memorial and was greatly enraged; that same day Zhan was removed from the chief-minister post and appointed Acting Minister of Justice, Associate Chief Minister, Chief of Jiangling, and Jingnan Military Commissioner. He was again demoted Prefect of Kang and transferred in measure to Prefect of Guo. He entered court as Crown Prince Guest serving in the branch office. Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Zheng Tian, Right Remonstrator Gao Xiang, Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer Yang Zhizhi, Director in the Ministry of Rites Wei Xu, Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of War Zhang Yan, Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Justice Cui Yanrong, and Censor-in-Chief Sun Huang—all because of close friendship with Zhan—were demoted and sent away. Chief of the Capital Wen Zhang took poison and died.
108
劉瑑者，彭城人。 祖璠，父煟。 瑑，開成初進士擢第。 會昌末，累遷尚書郎、知制誥，正拜中書舍人。 大中初，轉刑部侍郎。 瑑精於法律，選大中以前二百四十四年制敕可行用者二千八百六十五條，分為六百四十六門，議其輕重，別成一家法書，號《大中統類》，奏行用之。 出為河南尹，遷檢校工部尚書、汴州刺史、宣武軍節度使。 十一年五月，加檢校禮部尚書、太原尹、北都留守、河東節度觀察等使。 其年十二月入朝，拜戶部侍郎，判度支。 尋以本官同平章事，領使如故。 十二年，累加集賢殿大學士。 罷相，又歷方鎮，卒。 弟頊，亦登進士第。
Liu Zhuan was a native of Pengcheng. His grandfather was Fan and his father Wei. Zhuan, at the beginning of Kaicheng passed the jinshi selection. At the end of Huichang he was repeatedly promoted Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Drafting Officer for Proclamations, and formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. At the beginning of Dazhong he was transferred Vice Minister of Justice. Zhuan was skilled in law; he selected from two hundred forty-four years before Dazhong two thousand eight hundred sixty-five enforceable edicts and orders, divided them into six hundred forty-six categories, weighed their severity, and formed a separate legal work called Comprehensive Categories of the Dazhong Era, which he memorialized for use. He was sent out Chief of Henan, transferred Acting Minister of Public Works, Prefect of Bian, and Xuanwu Military Commissioner. In the fifth month of the eleventh year he was added Acting Minister of Rites, Chief of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Garrison Commander, and Hedong Military Commissioner and Observer. In the twelfth month of that year he entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Revenue Bureau. Soon with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister and continued as commissioner. In the twelfth year he was repeatedly added Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. Removed as chief minister he again passed through regional commands and died. His younger brother was Xu, who also passed the jinshi examination.
109
曹確，字剛中，河南人。 父景伯，貞元十九年進士擢第，又登制科。 確，開成二年登進士第，歷聘籓府。 入朝為侍御史，以工部員外郎知制誥，轉郎中，入內署為學士，正拜中書舍人，賜金紫，權知河南尹事。 入為兵部侍郎。 咸通五年，以本官同平章事，加中書侍郎、監修國史。
Cao Que, styled Gangzhong, was a native of Henan. His father Jingbo, in the nineteenth year of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi selection and also passed the special examination. Que, in the second year of Kaicheng passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly served in frontier headquarters. He entered court as Attending Censor, as Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Public Works directed proclamations, transferred Director, entered the inner secretariat as academician, was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat, granted gold and purple, and acted as Chief of Henan. He entered court as Vice Minister of War. In the fifth year of Xiantong, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister, added Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the National History.
110
確精儒術，器識謹重，動循法度。 懿宗以伶官李可及為威衛將軍，確執奏曰：「臣覽貞觀故事，太宗初定官品令，文武官共六百四十三員，顧謂房玄齡曰：『朕設此官員，以待賢士。 工商雜色之流，假令術逾儕類，止可厚給財物，必不可超授官秩，與朝賢君子比肩而立，同坐而食。』 太和中，文宗欲以樂官尉遲璋為王府率，拾遺竇洵直極諫，乃改授光州長史。 伏乞以兩朝故事，別授可及之官。」 帝不之聽。
Que was skilled in Confucian learning, his capacity and judgment careful and weighty, his actions always following law and measure. Emperor Yizong made the actor Li Keji Wei Guard General; Que resolutely submitted, saying, "Your subject has reviewed Zhenguan precedents: when Emperor Taizong first fixed the official rank statute, civil and military officials totaled six hundred forty-three posts; he looked at Fang Xuanling and said, 'We establish these official posts to await worthy men. For merchants, artisans, and miscellaneous classes—even if skill surpasses their kind—they may richly receive goods and wealth but must not be promoted beyond official rank to stand shoulder to shoulder with court worthies and gentlemen, sitting and eating together.' In the Taihe era Emperor Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang Rate of the Princely Household; Reminder Dou Xunzhi remonstrated to the utmost and he was instead appointed Chief Administrator of Guang. I humbly beg that by the two courts' precedents Keji be separately granted another office." The emperor did not listen.
111
可及善音律，尤能轉喉為新聲，音辭曲折，聽者忘倦。 京師屠沽效之，呼為「拍彈」。 同昌公主除喪後，帝與淑妃思念不已。 可及乃為《嘆百年舞曲》。 舞人珠翠盛飾者數百人，畫魚龍地衣，用官騑五千匹。 曲終樂闋，珠璣覆地，詞語淒惻，聞者涕流，帝故寵之。 嘗於安國寺作《菩薩蠻舞》，如佛降生，帝益憐之。 可及嘗為子娶婦，帝賜酒二銀樽，啟之非酒，乃金翠也。 人無敢非之者，唯確與中尉西門季玄屢論之，帝猶顧待不衰。 僖宗即位，崔彥昭奏逐之，死於嶺表。
Keji was skilled in music and especially able to turn the throat into new sounds; the words and tones were twisting and listeners forgot weariness. Butchers and wine sellers in the capital imitated this and called it "patting and plucking." After Princess Tongchang's mourning ended the emperor and Consort Shufei missed her endlessly. Keji then composed the dance "Lament for a Hundred Years." Several hundred dancers wore pearl and jade adornments; a carpet painted with fish and dragons was made using five thousand palace steeds. When the song ended and music ceased pearls and gems covered the ground; the words were mournful and listeners wept; the emperor therefore favored him. He once at Anguo Temple performed the "Bodhisattva Barbarian" dance like the Buddha's birth; the emperor favored him still more. Keji once arranged a marriage for his son; the emperor bestowed two silver goblets—when opened they were not wine but gold and kingfisher feathers. No one dared criticize except Que and Chief Eunuch Ximen Jixuan, who repeatedly argued; the emperor still favored him without decline. When Emperor Xizong acceded Cui Yanzhao memorialized to expel him and he died beyond the ranges.
112
確累加右僕射，判度支事。 在相位六年。 九年罷相，檢校司徒、平章事、潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度觀察等使。 以出師扞龐勛功，就加太子太師。 弟汾，亦進士登第，累官尚書郎、知制誥，正拜中書舍人。 出為河南尹，遷檢校工部尚書、許州刺史、忠武軍節度觀察等使。 入為戶部侍郎，判度支。 弟兄並列將相之任，人士榮之。
Que was repeatedly added Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Director of Revenue Bureau affairs. In the chief-minister position six years. In the ninth year he was removed as chief minister, appointed Acting Minister of Education, Associate Chief Minister, Prefect of Run, and Zhenhai Military Commissioner and Observer. For merit in dispatching troops against Pang Xun he was promoted Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince. Younger brother Fen also passed the jinshi examination, rose repeatedly to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer for Proclamations, and was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. He was sent out Chief of Henan, transferred Acting Minister of Public Works, Prefect of Xu, and Zhongwu Military Commissioner and Observer. He entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Revenue Bureau. The brothers both held posts of general and chief minister; scholars honored them.
113
確與畢諴俱以儒術進用，及居相位，廉儉貞苦，君子多之，稱為曹、畢。
Que and Bi Xian both advanced through Confucian learning; in the chief-minister position they were frugal, upright, and bitterly austere—gentlemen greatly esteemed them and called them Cao and Bi.
114
畢諴者，字存之，鄆州須昌人也。 伯祖構，高宗時吏部尚書。 構弟栩，酆王府司馬，生淩。 淩為汾州長史，生勻，為協律郎。 勻生諴，少孤貧，燃薪讀書，刻苦自勵。 既長，博通經史，尤能歌詩。 端愨好古，交遊不雜。 太和中，進士擢第，又以書判拔萃，尚書杜悰鎮許昌，辟為從事。 悰領度支，諴為巡官。 悰鎮揚州，又從之。 悰入相，諴為監察，轉侍御史。
Bi Xian, styled Cunzhi, was a native of Xuchang in Yan Prefecture. Great-uncle Gou served as Minister of Personnel in Emperor Gaozong's time. Gou's younger brother Xu was Prince of Feng's household marshal and begot Ling. Ling served as Chief Administrator of Fen and begot Yun, who was Harmonizing Law Officer. Yun begot Xian, who from youth was orphaned and poor, burned firewood to read books, and strove bitterly to encourage himself. When grown he was broadly versed in the classics and histories and especially skilled at song and poetry. Upright and fond of antiquity, his associations were not mixed. In the Taihe era he passed the jinshi selection and also distinguished himself in document judgment; Minister Du Cong governed Xuchang and summoned him as staff member. When Cong directed the Revenue Bureau Xian served as patrol officer. When Cong governed Yang Prefecture Xian followed him. When Cong entered the chief-minister post Xian served as Attending Censor and transferred Attending Censor.
115
武宗朝，宰相李德裕專政，出悰為東蜀節度。 悰之故吏，莫敢餞送問訊，唯諴無所顧慮，問遺不絕。 德裕怒，出諴為磁州刺史。 宣宗即位，德裕得罪，凡被譴者皆征還。 諴入為戶部員外郎，分司東都，歷駕部員外郎、倉部郎中。 故事，勢門子弟，鄙倉、駕二曹，居之者不悅。 唯諴受命，恬然恭遜，口無異言，執政多之。 改職方郎中，兼侍御史知雜。 其年。 召為翰林學士、中書舍人，遷刑部侍郎。
In Emperor Wuzong's court Chief Minister Li Deyu monopolized governance and sent Cong out as Eastern Shu Military Commissioner. Cong's former clerks dared not see him off or inquire after him; only Xian had no such concern and his visits and gifts never ceased. Deyu was angry and sent Xian out as Prefect of Ci. When Emperor Xuanzong acceded Deyu was condemned; all who had been punished were recalled. Xian entered court as Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Revenue, serving in the Eastern Capital branch, and passed through Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Tributary Carriages and Director in the Ministry of Granaries. By precedent sons of powerful gates despised the Granaries and Tributary Carriages bureaus; those who held them were displeased. Only Xian accepted appointment, calm and respectful, with no unusual words; those in power greatly approved. He was reassigned Director in the Ministry of War and concurrent Attending Censor with mixed duties. That year. He was summoned Hanlin Academician and Gentleman of the Secretariat and transferred Vice Minister of Justice.
116
自大中末，党項羌叛，屢擾河西。 宣宗召學士對邊事。 諴即援引古今，論列破羌之狀。 上悅，曰：「吾方擇能帥，安集河西，不期頗、牧在吾禁署，卿為朕行乎？」 諴忻然從命，即用諴為邠寧節度、河西供軍安撫等使。 諴至軍，遣使告喻叛徒，諸羌率化。 又以邊境禦戎，以兵多積谷為上策。 乃召募軍士，開置屯田，歲收谷三十萬石，省度支錢數百萬。 詔書嘉之，就加檢校工部尚書，移鎮澤潞，充昭義節度使。 二年，改太原尹、北都留守、河東節度使。 太原近胡，九姓為亂。 諴明賞罰，謹斥候，期年，諸部革心。 就加檢校尚書左僕射，移授汴州刺史，充宣武軍節度、宋亳汴觀察等使。 其年，入為戶部尚書，領度支。 月余，改禮部尚書，同平章事，累遷中書侍郎、兵部尚書、集賢大學士。
From the end of Dazhong the Tangut tribes rebelled and repeatedly disturbed Hexi. Emperor Xuanzong summoned academicians to discuss frontier affairs. Xian at once cited ancient and modern examples and laid out the form of breaking the Qiang. The emperor was pleased and said, "We are just choosing an able commander to settle and gather Hexi—unexpectedly Po and Mu are in Our forbidden secretariat; will you, minister, go for Us?" Xian gladly accepted the command and was at once appointed Binning Military Commissioner and Hexi Supply Army Pacification Commissioner. When Xian reached the army he sent envoys to announce and admonish the rebels; the various Qiang submitted to transformation. Also, for frontier defense against barbarians, accumulating much grain with many troops was the upper strategy. Then he recruited soldiers and opened garrison farms; yearly harvest was three hundred thousand shi of grain, saving several million strings from the Revenue Bureau. An edict praised this and he was promoted Acting Minister of Public Works and transferred to govern Ze-Lu as Zhaoyi Military Commissioner. In the second year he was reassigned Chief of Taiyuan, Northern Capital Garrison Commander, and Hedong Military Commissioner. Taiyuan is near the Hu; the nine surnames made disorder. Xian made rewards and punishments clear and kept scouts strict; within a year the various tribes changed heart. He was promoted Acting Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and transferred Prefect of Bian, serving as Xuanwu Military Commissioner and Song-Bo-Bian Observer. That year he entered court as Minister of Revenue and directed the Revenue Bureau. After more than a month he was reassigned Minister of Rites and Associate Chief Minister, repeatedly promoted Vice Director of the Secretariat, Minister of War, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
117
在相位三年，十月以疾固辭位，詔守兵部尚書，以其本官同平章事，出鎮河中。 十二月二十三日，卒於鎮，時年六十二。
In the chief-minister position three years; in the tenth month he firmly declined the post because of illness; an edict ordered him to serve as Minister of War with his existing office as Associate Chief Minister and sent him out to govern Hezhong. On the twenty-third day of the twelfth month he died in his command at age sixty-two.
118
諴謹重，長於文學，尤精吏術。 在相位，以同官任情不法，固辭而免，君子美之。
Xian was careful and weighty, skilled in literature, and especially expert in administrative technique. In the chief-minister position, because fellow ministers acted at will against law, he firmly declined and was removed—gentlemen praised this.
119
子紹顏、知顏，登進士第，累歷顯官。
His sons Shaoyan and Zhiyan passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly held prominent posts.
120
杜審權，字殷衡，京兆人也。 國初萊成公如晦六代孫。 祖佐，位終大理正。 佐生二子：元潁、元絳。
Du Shenquan, styled Yinheng, was a native of the capital district. He was sixth-generation descendant of Duke Lai Cheng Ruhui of the founding era. His grandfather Zuo ended as Director of the Court of Judicial Review. Zuo had two sons: Yuanying and Yuanjiang.
121
元潁，穆宗朝宰相。 絳位終太子賓客。 絳生二子：審權、蔚，並登進士第。
Yuanying was chief minister in Emperor Muzong's court. Jiang ended as Crown Prince Guest. Jiang had two sons: Shenquan and Wei, both of whom passed the jinshi examination.
122
審權，釋褐江西觀察判官，又以書判拔萃，拜右拾遺，轉左補闕。 大中初，遷司勛員外郎，轉郎中知雜。 又以本官知制誥，正拜中書舍人。 十年，權知禮部貢舉。 十一年，選士三十人，後多至達官。 正拜禮部侍郎。 其年冬，出為陜州大都督府長史、陜虢都團練觀察使，加檢校戶部尚書、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。
Shenquan, upon leaving office, served as judge of the Jiangxi Observation Commission; with distinguished performance in document judgment he was appointed Right Reminder and transferred Left Remonstrator. At the beginning of Dazhong he was transferred Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of War and Director with mixed duties. Again with his existing office he directed proclamations and was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. In the tenth year he acted as Director of the Ministry of Rites examination. In the eleventh year he selected thirty candidates; many later reached high office. He was formally appointed Vice Minister of Rites. That winter he was sent out Chief Administrator of Shaan Superior Protectorate, Shaan-Guo Training-and-Observation Commissioner, Acting Minister of Revenue, Chief of Hezhong, and Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner.
123
懿宗即位，召拜吏部尚書。 三年，以本官同平章事，累加門下侍郎、右僕射。 九年罷相，檢校司空，兼潤州刺史、鎮海軍節度使、蘇杭常等州觀察使。
When Emperor Yizong acceded he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel. In the third year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister and was repeatedly added Vice Director of the Secretariat and Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works. In the ninth year he was removed as chief minister, appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrent Prefect of Run, Zhenhai Military Commissioner, and Observer of Su, Hang, and Chang prefectures.
124
時徐州戍將龐勛自桂州擅還，據徐、泗，大擾淮南。 審權與淮南節度使令狐綯、荊南節度使崔鉉，奉詔出師，掎角討賊； 而浙西饋運不絕，繼破徐戎。 賊平，召拜尚書左僕射。 十一年，制曰：
At the time Xu garrison general Pang Xun on his own returned from Guiz Prefecture, held Xu and Si, and greatly disturbed Huainan. Shenquan with Huainan Military Commissioner Linghu Tao and Jingnan Military Commissioner Cui Xuan, by edict dispatched troops, pincered and attacked the bandits; yet Zhexi supply transport never ceased and they successively broke the Xu rebels. When the bandits were pacified he was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works. In the eleventh year an edict read:
125
數年以本官兼許州刺史、忠武軍節度觀察等使，入為太子太傅，分司東都。 卒，贈太師，謚曰德。
For several years with his existing office he was concurrent Prefect of Xu and Zhongwu Military Commissioner and Observer; he entered court as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, serving in the Eastern Capital branch, and died. He was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title De.
126
三子：讓能、彥林、弘徽。
Three sons: Rangneng, Yanlin, and Honghui.
127
讓能，咸通十四年登進士第，釋褐咸陽尉。 宰相王鐸鎮汴，奏為推官。 入為長安尉、集賢校理。 丁母憂，以孝聞。 服闋，淮南節度使劉鄴辟掌記室，得殿中，賜緋。 入為監察。 牛蔚鎮興元，奏為節度判官。 入為右補闕，歷侍御史、起居郎、禮部、兵部員外郎。 蕭遘領度支，以本官判度支案。
Rangneng, in the fourteenth year of Xiantong passed the jinshi examination and left office as Assistant Magistrate of Xianyang. Chief Minister Wang Duo governed Bian and memorialized him as investigating officer. He entered court as Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an and Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies. He entered mourning for his mother and was known for filial piety. When mourning ended Huainan Military Commissioner Liu Ye summoned him to manage the secretariat; he obtained Palace Attendance and was granted crimson. He entered court as Attending Censor. Niu Wei governed Xingyuan and memorialized him as military commission judge. He entered court as Right Remonstrator and passed through Attending Censor, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Outer Court Attendant in the Ministries of Rites and War. Xiao Zui directed the Revenue Bureau and with his existing office judged Revenue Bureau cases.
128
黃巢犯京師，奔赴行在，拜禮部郎中、史館修撰。 尋以本官知制誥，正拜中書舍人。 謝日，面賜金紫之服，尋召充翰林學士。 六飛在蜀，關東用兵，征發招懷，書詔雲委。
When Huang Chao attacked the capital he rushed to the traveling palace and was appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites and Historiographer. Soon with his existing office he directed proclamations and was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. On the day of thanks he was personally granted gold and purple robes; soon he was summoned Hanlin Academician. When the imperial carriage was in Shu, east of the Pass troops were raised; recruitment, conscription, and soothing filled edicts and proclamations.
129
讓能詞才敏速，筆無點竄，動中事機，僖宗嘉之，累遷戶部侍郎。 從駕還京，加禮部尚書，進階銀青光祿大夫，封建平縣開國子，食邑五百戶。 轉兵部尚書、學士承旨。
Rangneng's literary talent was quick; his brush needed no correction and he always hit the moment's need; Emperor Xizong praised this and repeatedly promoted him Vice Minister of Revenue. When the carriage returned to the capital he was added Minister of Rites, promoted Silver Light Grand Master of Palace Attendance, enfeoffed Baron of Jianping with a fief of five hundred households. He transferred Minister of War and Drafting Commissioner.
130
沙阤逼京師，僖宗蒼黃出幸。 是夜，讓能宿直禁中，聞難作，步出從駕。 出城十餘里，得遺馬一匹，無羈勒，以紳束首而乘之。 駕在鳳翔，朱玫兵遽至； 僖宗急幸寶雞，近臣唯讓能獨從。 翌日。 孔緯等六七人至。 邠師攻關，帝幸梁、漢，棧道為石協所毀，崎嶇險阻之間，不離左右。 帝顧謂之曰：「朕之失道，再致播遷。 險難之中，卿常在側，古所謂忠於所事，卿無負矣！」 讓能謝曰：「臣家世歷重任，蒙國厚恩，陛下不以臣愚，擢居近侍。 臨難茍免，臣之恥也； 獲扞牧圉，臣之幸也。」 至褒中，加金紫光祿大夫，改兵部侍郎，同平章事。
When Shatuo pressed the capital Emperor Xizong fled in haste. That night Rangneng was on night duty in the forbidden palace; hearing trouble arise he walked out to follow the carriage. More than ten li outside the city he obtained a stray horse; without bridle or reins he bound its head with his sash and rode it. When the carriage was at Fengxiang Zhu Mei's troops suddenly arrived; Emperor Xizong hastely went to Baoji; among close ministers only Rangneng followed alone. The next day. Kong Wei and six or seven others arrived. When Bin troops attacked the Pass the emperor went to Liang and Han; the plank road was destroyed by Shi Xie; amid rugged peril he never left the emperor's side. The emperor turned to him and said, "Our losing the Way twice caused exile. Amid danger and hardship you were always at Our side—what antiquity calls loyalty to one's charge; you have not failed Us!" Rangneng declined, saying, "Your subject's family for generations held heavy responsibility and received the state's thick grace; Your Majesty did not think your subject foolish and promoted him to close attendance. To escape in crisis would be your subject's shame; to be able to guard the ruler's carriage is your subject's fortune." When they reached Bao he was added Golden Light Grand Master of Palace Attendance, reassigned Vice Minister of War, and Associate Chief Minister.
131
時朱玫立襄王稱制，天下牧伯附之者十六七，貢賦殆絕。 朝士才十數人，行帑無寸金，衛兵不宿飽。 帝垂泣側席，無如之何。 讓能首陳大計，請以重臣使河中，諭王重榮以大義，果承詔請雪，以圖討逆。 京師平，拜特進、中書侍郎，兼兵部尚書、集賢殿大學士，進封襄陽郡開國公，食邑二千戶。 駕在鳳翔，李昌符作亂，倏然變起，讓能單步入侍。 時朝臣受偽署者眾，法司請行極法，以戒事君。 讓能固爭之，獲全者十七八。 昭宗纂嗣，賜「扶危啟運保乂功臣」，加開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射，封晉國公，增邑千戶，仍賜鐵券。 誅秦宗權，許、蔡平定，加司空、門下侍郎、監修國史。 昭宗郊禮畢，進位司徒、太清宮使、弘文館大學士、延資庫使、諸道鹽鐵轉運等使，加食邑一千戶。 明年，冊拜太尉，加食邑一千戶。
At the time Zhu Mei established the Prince of Xiang as regent; regional shepherds who joined numbered sixteen or seventeen and tribute nearly ceased. Court scholars numbered only a dozen or so; traveling treasury had not a foot of gold and guard soldiers did not sleep full. The emperor wept on the side of the mat and had no remedy. Rangneng first stated the great plan, requesting that a heavy minister be sent to Hezhong to explain the great principle to Wang Chongrong, who indeed accepted the edict and requested to clear the wrong and plan to attack the rebels. When the capital was pacified he was appointed Special Advancement, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of War, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang with a fief of two thousand households. When the carriage was at Fengxiang Li Changfu made disorder; suddenly mutiny arose and Rangneng entered alone to attend. At the time many court scholars accepted false appointments; the law office requested extreme punishment to warn those who serve rulers. Rangneng firmly argued and seventeen or eighteen were preserved. When Emperor Zhaozong succeeded he was granted "Meritorious Minister Who Supports Crisis, Initiates Fortune, and Preserves the Realm," added Grand Preceptor of the Palace, Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, enfeoffed Duke of Jin with an added fief of one thousand households, and still granted an iron certificate. When Qin Zongquan was executed Xu and Cai were pacified; he was added Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Supervisor of the National History. When Emperor Zhaozong completed the suburban sacrifice he was promoted Minister of Education, Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace, Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Culture, Commissioner of the Extension Capital Store, and Commissioner of Salt and Iron Transport for All Circuits, with fief increased one thousand households. The next year he was enfeoffed Grand Preceptor with fief increased one thousand households.
132
自大順已來，鳳翔李茂貞大聚兵甲，恃功驕恣。 會楊復恭走山南，茂貞欲兼有梁、漢之地，亟請問罪，詔未允而出師。 昭宗怒其專，不得已而從之。 及山南平，詔授以茂貞鎮興元，徐彥若鎮鳳翔，仍割果、閬兩州隸武定軍。 茂貞怒，上章論列，語辭不遜。 又與讓能書曰：
From Datong onward Li Maozhen of Fengxiang greatly gathered armor and weapons and relied on merit to be proud and unrestrained. When Yang Fugong fled to Shannan Maozhen wished to annex Liang and Han lands and urgently requested permission to punish guilt; the edict did not yet consent when he dispatched troops. Emperor Zhaozong was angry at his presumption and had no choice but to follow. When Shannan was pacified an edict granted Maozhen governorship of Xingyuan, Xu Yanruo governorship of Fengxiang, and still ceded Guo and Lang prefectures to the Wuding Army. Maozhen was angry and submitted a memorial arguing; his words were not deferential. He also wrote to Rangneng saying:
133
「今明公舍築入夢，投竿為師，踐履中臺，制臨外閫，不究興亡之理，罕聞沈斷之機。 蓋意有所不平，心有所未悟，輒思上問，願審臧謀。
"Now the eminent lord abandons building in dreams and casts the fishing rod to become commander, treads the middle terrace and controls the outer command—he does not examine the logic of rise and fall and rarely hears of resolute judgment. Surely intent is somewhat unequal and heart somewhat unenlightened; then one thinks to question above and wishes careful examination of hidden counsel.
134
竊見楊守亮擅舉干戈，阻艱西道，將圖割據，吞並東川。 居巴、幹為一窟豺狼，在梁、漢致十年荊棘。 果聞敗衄，尋挫兇狂。 既前去而不諧，思卻歸而無地。 當道與邠州見為隔絕綱運，方舉問罪兵師，忽聞朝廷授武定之雙旌，割果、閬之兩郡，未審是何名目？ 酬何功勞？ 紊大國之紀綱，蠹天子之州縣，非惟取笑於童稚，抑亦包羞於馬牛。 自謂奇謀，信為獨見。 伏慮是明公賞兇黨無君之輩，挫忠臣奉國之心。 要助奸邪，須摧正直。 又聞公切於保位，利在安家。 商量不自於中書剸割全通於內地。 雖知深奧，罕測津涯，亦聞駭異群情，頗，是喧騰眾口。」
I see Yang Shouliang on his own raising weapons, blocking the hard western route, intending to carve out territory and swallow Dongchuan. Dwelling in Ba and Qian as one den of wolves and jackals, in Liang and Han causing ten years of brambles. Indeed I heard of defeat and rout and soon checked fierce madness. Having gone forward without harmony, he thought to return but had no place. Our route and Bin Prefecture are now cut off from grain transport; just as punitive troops were raised I suddenly heard the court grant Wuding's double banners and cede Guo and Lang two prefectures—may I ask what title this is? Rewarding what merit? Disordering the great state's discipline and ruining the Son of Heaven's prefectures and counties—not only ridiculed by children but also shameful to oxen and horses. Calling it clever strategy—truly a view held alone. I fear the eminent lord rewards the unprincipled faction and frustrates the loyal ministers' spirit of serving the state. To aid the wicked one must crush the upright. I also hear the lord is eager to preserve position and profit lies in settling the family. Consultation not from within the Secretariat cut off and wholly granted to the inner lands. Though one knows depth and obscurity and rarely fathoms the ford's edge, I also hear alarm at the crowd's feelings and much clamor in the multitude's mouths."
135
其悖戾如此。
His perversity was thus.
136
京師百姓，聞茂貞聚兵甲，群情恟々，數千百人守闕門。 候中尉西門重遂出，擁馬論列曰：「乞不分割山南，請姑息鳳翔，與百姓為主。」 重遂曰：「此非吾事，出於宰相也。」 昭宗怒，詔讓能只在中書調發畫計，不歸第。 月余，宰相崔昭緯陰結邠、岐為城社，凡讓能出一言，即日達於茂貞、行瑜。 茂貞令健兒數百人，雜市人於街。 崔昭緯、鄭延昌歸第，市人擁肩輿訴曰：「岐帥無罪，幸相公不加討伐，致都邑不寧。」 二相輿中喻之曰：「大政聖上委杜太尉，吾等不預。」 市豪褰簾熟視，又不之識，因投瓦石，擊二相之輿。 崔、鄭下輿散走，匿身獲免。 是日，喪堂印公服，天子怒，捕魁首誅之，由是用兵之意愈堅。 京師之人，相與藏竄，嚴刑不能已。 讓能奏曰：「陛下初臨大寶，國步未安。 自艱難以來，且行貞元故事，姑息籓鎮。 茂貞邇在國門，不宜起怨。 臣料此時未可行也。」 帝曰：「政刑削弱，詔令不出城門，此賈生慟哭之際也。 又《書》不雲乎？ 藥不瞑眩，厥疾弗瘳。 朕不能孱孱度日，坐觀淩弱。 卿為我主張調發，用兵吾委諸王。」 讓能對曰：「陛下憤籓臣之倔強，必欲強幹弱枝以隆王室，此則中外大臣所宜戮力，以成陛下之誌，不宜獨任微臣。」 帝曰：「卿位居元輔，與朕同休共戚，無宜避事。」 讓能泣辭曰：「臣待罪臺司，未乞骸骨者，思有以報國恩耳，安敢愛身避事？ 況陛下之心，憲祖之誌也。 但時有所不便，勢有所必然。 他日臣雖受晁錯之誅，但不足以殄七國之患，敢不奉詔，繼之以死！」
Capital commoners, hearing Maozhen gathered armor and weapons, were alarmed; several thousand hundreds guarded the palace gate. Waiting for Chief Eunuch Ximen Zhongsui to come out, they surrounded his horse and argued, saying, "We beg not to divide Shannan; please soothe Fengxiang and be master for the common people." Zhongsui said, "This is not my affair—it comes from the chief minister." Emperor Zhaozong was angry and edicted that Rangneng remain only in the Secretariat to dispatch and plan and not return to his residence. After more than a month Chief Minister Cui Zhaowei secretly allied with Bin and Qi as a city altar; whenever Rangneng spoke one word it reached Maozhen and Xingyu the same day. Maozhen ordered several hundred strong men mixed with market people in the streets. When Cui Zhaowei and Zheng Yanchang returned home market people surrounded the shoulder carriage and pleaded, saying, "The Qi commander is innocent; we beg the chief ministers not to add punishment and cause the capital to be unsettled." The two chief ministers explained from within the carriage, saying, "Great affairs the Sacred One entrusts to Grand Preceptor Du—we do not participate." Market bullies lifted the curtain and looked closely yet did not recognize them; therefore they threw tiles and stones and struck the two chief ministers' carriages. Cui and Zheng left the carriage and scattered fleeing; they hid and escaped. That day they lost hall seals and official robes; the Son of Heaven was angry, captured ringleaders and executed them—therefore the will to use troops grew firmer. Capital people hid together; severe punishment could not stop it. Rangneng submitted, saying, "Your Majesty has just acceded to the great treasure and the state's step is not yet settled. Since hardship we have for a time followed the Zhenyuan precedent, soothing the frontier commands. Maozhen is near the capital gate—it is not fitting to raise resentment. Your subject calculates that at this time it cannot yet be done." The emperor said, "Government and punishment are weakened; edicts do not leave the city gate—this is the moment for Jia Yi's wailing. Also does not the Book say? Medicine that does not cause dizziness will not cure the illness. We cannot live feebly day by day and sit watching encroachment. You plan dispatch and mobilization for Us; in using troops We entrust it to the princes." Rangneng replied, "Your Majesty resents the frontier ministers' stubbornness and must strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches to elevate the royal house—then inside and outside the great ministers should unite strength to fulfill Your Majesty's will; it is not fitting to entrust this alone to your humble subject." The emperor said, "You stand at the summit of ministers and share with Us joy and sorrow—there is no reason to avoid affairs." Rangneng wept and declined, saying, "Your subject awaits punishment at the censorate and has not yet requested old bones because he thinks to repay national grace—how dare he cherish body and avoid affairs? Moreover Your Majesty's heart is Emperor Xianzong's will. But sometimes the time is inconvenient and momentum has its necessity. Another day your subject may receive Chao Cuo's execution—but it will not suffice to extinguish the Seven States' trouble; I dare not refuse the edict and will follow with death!"
137
景福二年秋，上以嗣覃王為招討使，神策將李鐬副之，率禁軍三萬，送彥若赴鎮。 崔昭緯密與邠、鳳結托，心害讓能； 言討伐非上意，出於大尉也。 九月，茂貞出軍逆戰，王師敗於盩啡。 岐兵乘勝至三橋。 讓能奏曰：「臣固預言之矣。 請歸罪於臣，可以紓難。」 上涕下不能已，曰：「與卿訣矣。」 即日貶為雷州司戶。 茂貞在臨臯驛，請誅讓能。 尋賜死，時年五十三。 駕自石門還京，念讓能之冤，追贈太師。
In the autumn of the second year of Jingfu the emperor made Prince of Siyin campaign commander with Shence General Li Hui as deputy, leading thirty thousand forbidden troops to escort Yanruo to his command. Cui Zhaowei secretly colluded with Bin and Feng; he hated Rangneng in heart; he said the punitive campaign was not the emperor's intent but came from the Grand Preceptor. In the ninth month Maozhen sent troops to meet in battle and the imperial army was defeated at Zhouzhi. Qi troops seized victory and reached the Three Bridges. Rangneng submitted, saying, "Your subject indeed foretold this beforehand. Please return guilt to your subject and difficulty may be eased." The emperor wept without stopping, saying, "We take leave of you." That same day he was demoted Assistant Administrator of Lei. Maozhen was at Lingao Post and requested Rangneng's execution. Soon he was ordered to die at age fifty-three. When the carriage returned from Shimen to the capital the emperor remembered Rangneng's injustice and posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
138
子光乂、曉，以父枉橫，不求聞達。 曉入梁，位亦至宰輔。
His sons Guangyi and Xiao, because of their father's wrongful death, did not seek renown. Xiao entered Liang and also reached chief minister.
139
彥林、弘徽，乾符中相次登進士第。 彥林，光化中累官至尚書郎、知制誥，拜中書舍人。 天祐初，為御史中丞。
Yanlin and Honghui in the Qianfu era successively passed the jinshi examination. Yanlin, in the Guanghua era rose repeatedly to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer for Proclamations and was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. At the beginning of Tianyou he served as Censor-in-Chief.
140
弘徽，累官至中書舍人，遷戶部侍郎，充弘文館學士判館事，與兄同日被害。
Honghui rose repeatedly to Gentleman of the Secretariat, transferred Vice Minister of Revenue, and served as Hanlin Academician directing the Hall of Illustrious Culture; he and his elder brother were killed the same day.
141
劉鄴，字漢籓，潤州句容人也。 父三復，聰敏絕人，幼善屬文。 少孤貧，母有廢疾，三復丐食供養，不離左右，久之不遂鄉賦。
Liu Ye, styled Hanfan, was a native of Jurong in Run Prefecture. His father Sanfu was extraordinarily intelligent from youth and skilled at composing prose. Orphaned young and poor, his mother had crippling illness; Sanfu begged food to support her and never left her side; for a long time he did not follow the local examination.
142
長慶中，李德裕拜浙西觀察使，三復以德裕禁密大臣，以所業文詣郡幹謁。 德裕閱其文，倒屣迎之，乃辟為從事，管記室。 母亡，哀毀殆不勝喪。 德裕三為浙西，凡十年，三復皆從之。 太和中，德裕輔政，用為員外郎。 居無何，罷相，復鎮浙西，三復從之。 汝州刺史劉禹錫以宗人遇之。 深重其才，嘗為詩贈三復，序曰：「從弟三復，三為浙右從事，凡十余年。 往年主公入相，薦用登朝，中復從公之京口，未幾而罷。 昨以尚書員外郎奉使至潞，旋承新命，改轅而東。 三從公皆在舊地，征諸故事，夐無其比，因賦詩餞別以誌之。」 又從德裕歷滑臺、西蜀、揚州，累遷御史中丞。 會昌中，德裕用事，自諫議、給事拜刑部侍郎、弘文館學士判館事。
In the Changqing era Li Deyu became Zhexi Observation Commissioner; Sanfu, because Deyu was a forbidden-secretariat great minister, took his literary work to the command to seek audience. Deyu read his writing, went out with shoes reversed to welcome him, and summoned him as staff member managing the secretariat. When his mother died his grief and destruction nearly exceeded what mourning could bear. Deyu three times governed Zhexi; for ten years Sanfu always followed him. In the Taihe era when Deyu assisted governance Sanfu was used as Outer Court Attendant. Within not long he was removed as chief minister, again governed Zhexi, and Sanfu followed him. Prefect of Ru Liu Yuxi treated him as a clansman. Deeply valuing his talent, he once composed a poem presenting it to Sanfu with a preface saying, "Cousin Sanfu, three times staff member of Zheyou, altogether more than ten years. In former years when the lord entered the chief-minister post he was recommended and used to ascend court; again he followed the lord to Jingkou and before long was removed. Yesterday as Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of Revenue he was sent on mission to Lu; soon he received new appointment and changed carriage east. Three times following the lord all in old places—consulting precedents, far without parallel—therefore I compose a farewell poem to record it." Again he followed Deyu through Hua Platform, Western Shu, and Yang Prefecture and was repeatedly promoted Censor-in-Chief. In the Huichang era when Deyu held power, from Remonstrator and Supervising Censor he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Hanlin Academician directing the Hall of Illustrious Culture.
143
朝廷用兵誅劉稹，澤潞既平。 朝議以劉從諫妻裴氏是裴問之妹，欲原之。 法司定罪，以劉稹之叛，裴以酒食會潞州將校妻女，泣告以固逆謀。 三復奏曰：
The court used troops to execute Liu Zhen and Ze-Lu was pacified. Court discussion held that Liu Congjian's wife Lady Pei was younger sister of Pei Wen; they wished to pardon her. The law office fixed guilt: because Liu Zhen rebelled Lady Pei with wine and food feasted Lu Prefecture officers' wives and daughters and wept telling them to fix the treason plan. Sanfu submitted, saying:
144
從之。 三復未幾病卒。
The request was granted. Before long Sanfu died of illness.
145
鄴六七歲能賦詩，李德裕尤憐之，與諸子同硯席師學。 大中初，德裕貶逐，鄴無所依，以文章客遊江、浙。 每有制作，人皆稱誦。 高元裕廉察陜虢，署為團練推官，得秘書省校書郎。 咸通初，劉瞻、高璩居要職，以故人子薦為左拾遺，召充翰林學士，轉尚書郎中知制誥，正拜中書舍人、戶部侍郎、學士承旨。
Ye at six or seven could compose poetry; Deyu especially cherished him and with his sons shared desk and teacher. At the beginning of Dazhong when Deyu was demoted and sent away Ye had nowhere to rely and with writings lodged as guest traveling Jiang and Zhe. Whenever he had compositions people all praised and recited them. Gao Yuanyu inspected Shaan and Guo and retained him as training commission investigating officer; he obtained proofreader of the Secretariat. At the beginning of Xiantong Liu Zhan and Gao Cong held important posts and as old friend's son recommended him Left Reminder; he was summoned Hanlin Academician, transferred Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer for Proclamations, formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and Vice Minister of Revenue, and Drafting Commissioner.
146
鄴以李德裕貶死珠崖，大中朝以令狐綯當權，累有赦宥，不蒙恩例。 懿宗即位，綯在方鎮，屬郊天大赦，鄴奏論之曰：「故崖州司戶參軍李德裕，其父吉甫，元和中以直道明誠，高居相位，中外鹹理，訏謨有功。 德裕以偉望宏才，繼登臺袞； 險夷不易，勁正無群。 稟周勃厚重之姿，慕楊秉忠貞之節。 頃以微累，竄於遐荒，既迫衰殘，竟歸冥寞。 其子燁坐貶象州立山縣尉。 去年遇陛下布惟新之命，覃作解之恩，移授郴州郴縣尉，今已歿於貶所。 倘德裕猶有親援，可期振揚，微臣固不敢上論，以招浮議。 今骨肉將盡，生涯已空，皆傷棨戟之門，遽作荊榛之地； 孤骨未歸於塋兆，一男又沒於湘江。 特乞聖明，俯垂哀湣，俾還遺骨，兼賜贈官。 上弘錄舊之仁，下激徇公之節。」 詔從之。
Because Li Deyu was demoted to die at Zhuya, in the Dazhong court Linghu Tao held power and though amnesties repeatedly came he did not receive the grace precedent. When Emperor Yizong acceded Tao was in a regional command; at the suburban great amnesty Ye submitted arguing, saying, "The former Assistant Administrator of Yai Prefecture Li Deyu—his father Jifu in the Yuanhe era with straight way and bright sincerity stood high in the chief-minister post; inside and outside all were ordered and his grand counsel had merit. Deyu with great expectation and vast talent successively ascended the terrace and chief-minister's robe; through danger and ease he did not change, stern and upright without clique. He bore Zhou Bo's weighty bearing and admired Yang Bing's loyal and pure integrity. Recently because of slight trouble he was exiled to distant wilderness; already pressed by decline and infirmity he finally returned to the dark unknown. His son Ye because of demotion served as Assistant Magistrate of Xiang Prefecture's Lishan County. Last year encountering Your Majesty's renewal decree and broad pardon grace he was transferred Assistant Magistrate of Chen Prefecture's Chen County; now he has already died in the place of demotion. If Deyu still had kin to rely on, restoration could be expected; your humble subject indeed dare not argue upward lest it invite floating criticism. Now flesh and bone are nearly exhausted and livelihood already empty—all wounding the halberd gate, suddenly becoming thorn and bramble land; lonely bones have not returned to the tomb mound and one son again perished in the Xiang River. I specially beg the sage brightness to bend and show pity, enabling return of the remaining bones and also granting posthumous office. Above to expand the grace of recording the old; below to stimulate the integrity of giving oneself for the public." An edict followed this.
147
鄴尋以本官領諸道鹽鐵轉運使。 其年同平章事，判度支，轉中書侍郎，兼吏部尚書，累加太清宮使、弘文館大學士。 僖宗即位，蕭倣、崔彥昭秉政，素惡鄴，乃罷鄴知政事，檢校尚書左僕射、同平章事、揚州大都督府長史、淮南節度使。 是日鄴押班宣麻竟，通事引鄴內殿謝，不及笏記，鄴自敘十余句語云：「霖雨無功，深愧代天之用； 煙霄失路，未知歸骨之期。」 帝為之惻然。
Ye soon with his existing office directed Salt and Iron Transport for All Circuits. That year he became Associate Chief Minister, Director of the Revenue Bureau, transferred Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Minister of Personnel, and was repeatedly added Commissioner of the Great Pure Palace and Grand Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Culture. When Emperor Xizong acceded Xiao Fang and Cui Yanzhao directed governance and always disliked Ye; they removed Ye from governing affairs and appointed Acting Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Associate Chief Minister, Chief Administrator of Yang Superior Protectorate, and Huainan Military Commissioner. That day when Ye finished proclaiming the edict as ranking officer the usher led Ye inside the hall to give thanks; without tablet notes Ye himself narrated more than ten sentences, saying, "Long rain without merit—deeply ashamed at substituting for heaven's use; cloud ladder lost the way—not knowing the day bones return." The emperor was moved for him.
148
黃巢渡淮而南，詔以浙西高駢代還，尋除風翔尹、鳳翔隴右節度使，以疾辭，拜左僕射。 巢賊犯長安，鄴從駕不及，與崔沆、豆盧瑑匿於金吾將軍張直方之家。 旬日，賊嚴切追捕，三人夜竄； 為賊所得，迫以偽命，稱病不應，俱為賊所害。
When Huang Chao crossed the Huai south an edict had Gao Pian of Zhexi replace him; soon he was removed Chief of Fengxiang and Fengxiang-Long Right Military Commissioner; he pleaded illness and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works. When the bandits attacked Chang'an Ye could not follow the carriage and with Cui Hang and Dou Luzhan hid in General of the Golden Guard Zhang Zhifang's house. After ten days the bandits strictly pursued; the three men fled by night; they were seized by bandits, forced with false appointments, claimed illness and did not respond, and all were harmed by bandits.
149
豆盧瑑者，河東人。 祖願，父籍，皆以進士擢第。 瑑，大中十三年亦登進士科。 咸通末，累遷兵部員外郎，轉戶部郎中知制誥，召充翰林學士，正拜中書舍人。 乾符中，累遷戶部侍郎、學士承旨。 六年，與吏部侍郎崔沆同日拜平章事。 宣制曰，大風雷雨拔樹。 左丞韋蟾與王瑑善，往賀之。 瑑言及雷雨之異，蟾曰：「此應相公為霖作解之祥也。」 瑑笑答曰：「霖何甚耶？」 及巢賊犯京師，從僖宗出開遠門，為盜所制，乃匿於張直方之家，遇害。 識者以風雷，不令之兆也。
Dou Luzhan was a native of Hedong. His grandfather Yuan and father Ji both passed the jinshi selection. Zhan, in the thirteenth year of Dazhong also passed the jinshi examination. At the end of Xiantong he was repeatedly promoted Outer Court Attendant in the Ministry of War, transferred Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Drafting Officer for Proclamations, summoned Hanlin Academician, and formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat. In the Qianfu era he was repeatedly promoted Vice Minister of Revenue and Drafting Commissioner. In the sixth year he and Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Cui Hang on the same day became Associate Chief Minister. When the edict was proclaimed, great wind, thunder, and rain uprooted trees. Left Vice Director Wei Chan was friendly with Wang Zhuan and went to congratulate him. Zhan spoke of the thunder and rain anomaly; Chan said, "This responds to the chief minister making rain and releasing the oath as auspicious." Zhan smiled and replied, "How very much rain!" When the bandits attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong out the Kaiyuan Gate, was seized by robbers, then hid in Zhang Zhifang's house and met harm. Observers held the wind and thunder an omen of ill appointment.
150
弟瓚、璨，皆進士登第，累歷清要。 瓚子革，中興位亦至宰輔。
Younger brothers Zan and Can both passed the jinshi examination and repeatedly held pure and important posts. Zan's son Ge in the Restoration also reached chief minister.
151
史臣曰：近代衣冠人物，門族昌盛，從、颋之後，實富名流。 而彥曾屬徐亂之秋，胤接李亡之數，計則繆矣，天可逃乎？ 楊、劉、曹畢諸族，門非世胄，位以藝升，伏膺典墳，俯拾青紫。 而收得位求侈，以至敗名。 行己飭躬，此為深誡！ 杜氏三世輔相，太尉陷於橫流，臨難忘身，可為流涕。
The historian says: In recent times among robed gentry and persons, clans flourished; after Cong and Ting there were truly many famous streams. Yet Yanzeng belonged to the season of Xu disorder and Yin met the fate of Li's fall—the plan was wrong; can heaven be escaped? The Yang, Liu, Cao, and Bi clans—gates not of hereditary nobility, ranks risen through art, bowing to the classics and picking up purple and green. Yet Shou obtaining rank sought extravagance until he ruined his name. To discipline oneself and adorn the person—this is a deep warning! The Du clan for three generations assisted as chief ministers; the Grand Preceptor fell in the cross current—facing difficulty without forgetting self, one may weep for this.
152
贊曰：漢代荀、陳，我朝崔、杜。 有子有弟，多登宰輔。 裴士改節，楊子敗名。 膏粱移性，信而有征。
The praise says: Han had Xun and Chen; our court has Cui and Du. With sons and with younger brothers, many ascended chief minister. Pei the scholar changed his nature; Yang the son ruined his name. Rich food shifts character—believed and there is proof.
